title: espOS board
description: One physical board a boat owner can buy or already owns. Boards are curated: list one only when someone has run espOS firmware on it. Firmware projects refer to boards by id; the flasher shows this entry, with its photo, when someone picks a board or a use case.

id.description: Must equal the filename without .json, and the id projects use in their boards array.

vendor.description: Who makes it, as printed on the box: "Waveshare". "Various" for a generic board many shops sell.

model.description: The vendor's model or part number, as on the shop page.

name.description: What the flasher shows. Fills in a project board's name when the project gives none.

package.description: The chip or module variant, e.g. ESP32-S3R8. Embedded flash and PSRAM show in it, and the flasher can read it from the chip.

features.description: What the hardware has, in the words use cases match on. A radio reached through a co-processor (the P4's ESP32-C6) counts.

usbBridge.description: The USB-to-serial chip, which a browser can read before anything is flashed. A hint toward this board, never proof: many boards share a bridge.

factoryApps.description: Project names the vendor's factory firmware reports in its app description, so a board straight from the box can be recognised.

image.description: A photo of the board. Only one whose licence allows it; say whose it is in imageCredit.

notes.description: Cautions that hold whatever the firmware: power, antennas, jumpers.
